intro: This is a mantra from the **Rigveda** (Rigveda 10.129.1, Nasadiya Sukta). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **नासदासीन्नो सदासीत्तदानीं नासीद्रजो नो व्योमा परो यत् । किमावरीवः कुह कस्य शर्मन्नम्भः किमासीद्गहनं गभीरम् ॥**
Then there was neither being nor non-being, no realm of space, no sky beyond. What covered it, where, in whose keeping? Was there deep, unfathomable water?
The Rigveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: Then there was neither being nor non-being, no realm of space, no sky beyond. What covered it, where, in whose keeping? Was there deep, unfathomable water?
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
